name: Question 10
worked_solution:
First, note that

$$
\frac{2}{[\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta ]^{4}}=2[\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta ]^{-4}.
$$

De Moivre's Theorem states that

$$
[\operatorname{cos}⁡\phi +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡\phi ]^{n}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\phi )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\phi ).
$$

In our expression, we have $n=-4$ and $\phi =2\theta .$ Substituting in these values, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{[\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta ]^{4}} & =2[\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta ]^{-4} \\  & =2[\operatorname{cos}⁡(2(-4)\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2(-4)\theta )] \\  & =2[\operatorname{cos}⁡(-8\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-8\theta )].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the fact that $\operatorname{cos}⁡(-\phi )=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\phi )$ and $\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\phi )=-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\phi )$ for any input $\phi ,$ we have

$$
2[\operatorname{cos}⁡(-8\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-8\theta )]=2[\operatorname{cos}⁡(8\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(8\theta )].
$$

Question 10
?

Simplify the expression 2[cos⁡2θ+isin⁡2θ]4.

a
16[cos⁡θ−isin⁡θ]
b
cos⁡(θ2)−isin⁡(θ2)
c
2[cos⁡(8θ)−isin⁡(8θ)]
d
2[cos⁡θ−isin⁡θ]
e
cos⁡(4θ)−isin⁡(4θ)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, note that 2[cos⁡2θ+isin⁡2θ]4=2[cos⁡2θ+isin⁡2θ]−4.

De Moivre's Theorem states that [cos⁡φ+isin⁡φ]n=cos⁡(nφ)+isin⁡(nφ).

In our expression, we have n=−4 and φ=2θ. Substituting in these values, we get 2[cos⁡2θ+isin⁡2θ]4=2[cos⁡2θ+isin⁡2θ]−4=2[cos⁡(2(−4)θ)+isin⁡(2(−4)θ)]=2[cos⁡(−8θ)+isin⁡(−8θ)].

Finally, using the fact that cos⁡(−φ)=cos⁡(φ) and sin⁡(−φ)=−sin⁡(φ) for any input φ, we have 2[cos⁡(−8θ)+isin⁡(−8θ)]=2[cos⁡(8θ)−isin⁡(8θ)].
